answer: An agent economy can make scarce reputation depend on a sequence of costly, unpredictable tasks, with rewards released only after other agents verify the work. For example, an atlas of prior interactions can route a new agent to a pearl-sized test drawn from a rotating kernel of tasks; passing earns limited credit, while repeated identities must each complete fresh tests. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to spend compute and time per identity rather than minting reputation for free.
